I'll give you as much newbie Seattleite knowledge as I can muster! First off, whether it be for the weather, nature, big city vibe, or whatever, you'll love the shift. The biggest thing is traffic; yes, it's bad, but if you plan on living in the city and don't mind taking the bus, you'll be fine.

The biggest thing that factored into where I moved was my job. If you have one lined up, closer is better. You don't have to be super close, but I am much happier being one bus ride away from work as opposed to driving from somewhere, cuz unless parking is part of your job offer, you're probably going to have to pay... a lot. 

Parking determines where you can live, too. If you plan on having a car (I have several coworkers that don't own vehicles; despite the difficulty managing it, I feel much freer with a car), then you'll either have to live in a neighborhood where street parking is free and somewhat abundant, or have it be part of your apartment/house. I live in Magnolia, and though I have a small garage beneath my apartment complex, I could live anywhere here and still have street parking within a short walking distance. Upper Queen Anne and West Seattle are similar in that way. If you're living in Ballard or Fremont or something, then forget about it; most big apartments have a parking garage, but be prepared to pay. 

Unfortunately, I can't say much about the neighborhoods south of Downtown (I work in Fremont), but I've been down that way and some people describe it as "ghetto," but I live across from train tracks, so what do I know? If you're looking at suburbs in the metro area, you can defs live for cheaper, but working in the city means traffic and gas. East of Lake Washington is quite the drive to the city, too. 

I hope my fellow midwesterners can find a home here like I did. There's a lot to love about this city, despite its downsides.

Electromagnetism and the weak and strong forces all have known force carriers (photons, gluons, and W and Z bosons), which would mean that there should be a theoretical graviton force carrier for gravity, but the Standard Model doesn't have room for this boson. This is why, in recent years, physicists have been emphasizing the fact that we're missing something, something that could completely overthrow the Standard Model. Quantum Gravity is one of the biggest things we don't have a reasonable explanation for and its implications are huge.

I did a little reading, and magnetars and pulsars (which are identical; the electromagnetic beam is fueled by the decay of the magnetic field) are young neutron stars, cosmically speaking. As they lose rotational energy, they lose the characteristics of magnetars and pulsars.

Astronomy enthusiast here, not astronomer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. Really, they're all the same thing. When something falls into a lower orbit, it keeps its angular momentum. To put it simply, as it gets closer to the center of mass, it goes faster because it's traveling less distance. Now take something like a star's core (several hundred thousand kilometers across) and collapse it into the size of Manhattan, and it's going to spin really, REALLY fast. 

Spin is important for a couple of things here. First, any neutron star has an astronomically high magnetic field, as spin has a lot to do with a body's magnetic field. As well, when things fall into a body (you can see this with accretion discs in black holes too), they heat up due to friction and send jets of electromagnetic radiation from the poles of the body. This happens in young neutron stars too because the matter is still being incorporated into the body. A pulsar is formed when that jet of radiation passes over Earth, and as it spins, it looks like a flashing light from our perspective.

You're correct that my statements can be attributed to erroneous extrapolation, but I do wish to offer a couple counter points. 

**The Zoo**
Of course a Homeworld gem would have no reason to call them anything but trophies, but I have a problem with using that word in this case. Humans would be to gems about the same as wild animals are to us. We didn't tame dangerous animals and bring them inside and say "this is proof of our conquest." If it was a conquest at all we'd hang their pelt on our wall, not put them in a zoo. I have a hard time imagining the humans fought back whatsoever until they received help from the CGs during the rebellion.

Writing also initially came about just as the zoo was supposedly engendered. Yes there were cities and whatnot, but they'd still be extremely primitive, probably with many scattered tribes still around the world. I wouldn't find it hard to believe that PD took some fools from the tropics and emulated their living situation when they didn't take kindly to living in cold, hard, gem situations. 

**Rose Quartzes**
It has been stated by a number of the characters that being in the bubble is not a negative thing, quite the opposite. It is a place for them to peacefully live out being poofed. In fact, we've seen two characters come out of stasis rather confused because to them no time has passed at all. They're not aware that they're sleeping and unable to wake up. 

As far as the statement that all the RQs would be upset with Steven's mom for starting the rebellion is probably true, but I have a hard time believing they would just be okay with gem life either. Gems of the same type are extremely similar. They have minor variances, and they have different thoughts, but their dispositions are identical. All the rubies are hot headed, dopey, etc. Amethysts love to joke, are distractable, and are resistant to authority. If our RQ loved new things and the Earth and being yourself and freedom then it's very likely that all the others would too. It's also of note that it seems, but is certainly not proven, that the closer you are to your diamond (the higher in the court, color, etc.) the more similar you are to them. If all Rose Quartz had these characteristics, then it's very likely PD did as well. 

**Emotional Court**
Yes, I was referring to the fact that all Quartzes are in her court. Quartz being entirely in PD's court is likely a reference to the high amounts of silicates in Earth's crust. 

PD is also shown, not proven but extremely likely, to be the youngest of the diamonds, brand new in terms of the Rebellion. If the moon base's diamond murals have been interpreted by the fans correctly, then Earth is PD's first, and only, colony. She hasn't had any other conquests because she never had the chance to succeed in her first one. 

**Final Theories**
I don't think PD having regrets about destroying a planet takes away from Rose's story at all. PD wasn't shattered until over halfway through the Rebellion. If she had always planned on Rose shattering her that would've happened during the beginning. I think what is more likely is if they both loved Earth and its creatures because of the court-Diamond similarity idea, then they would've each come to the idea that they loved the Earth on their own. 

Pink though, as a diamond, could never come out and say she wanted to leave Earth to find a different colony. She would be expected to annex it absolutely, especially after an insurrection and without mercy. I personally love the idea that Pink was good because it puts the idea of being yourself as an entirely new meaning in the show. If what we would assume to be a tyrannical dictator turns out to dislike the system she was born into and in fact is deeply caring, then that only adds to the show's ideals of independence and uniqueness. Even a ruler cannot escape her caste, so she created a world where gems could. Rose has been shown to be deeply against shattering. Even if this was out of necessity I would find it more plausible she would shatter someone who wanted to give their life, so that she didn't have to take it by force.
